votes.evidence: Premise traced from callers and found false. `find_signal_implementation_run` gates on `task.signal_report_id`, i.e. the `Task.signal_report` FK (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:508, :514). The cited `TaskRunCreateRequestSerializer.signal_report_id` CharField (products/tasks/backend/presentation/serializers.py:1746-1751) is consumed only by `run_task` (facade/api.py:4306), which loads an EXISTING task via `_visible_task_qs(...).filter(id=task_id).first()` (api.py:4325) and puts the string into `runtime_state_fields` -> `extra_state` (api.py:4405-4413, 4476-4489). `extra_state` only becomes `run.state` via `task.create_run(..., extra_state=extra_state)`; it never writes `task.signal_report`. The two sibling CharFields (serializers.py:1926 on `TaskRunBootstrapCreateRequestSerializer`, :2240 on `TaskRunResumeRequestSchemaSerializer`) follow the same run-state-only path in `bootstrap_task_run` (api.py:3002, task from `_get_task_for_run_control` at :3024, value into extra_state at :3047-3062). The only user-facing writer of the FK is `TaskWriteSerializer.signal_report`, a `PrimaryKeyRelatedField` (serializers.py:435-440) guarded by `validate_signal_report` which rejects reports from another team (serializers.py:611-614) and is set-once (api.py:3828-3830 pops it on update). `products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py` contains zero references to `signal_report`, so no view feeds a raw string into `create_and_run_task(signal_report_id=...)` (api.py:~880); its callers are all server-side signals flows (signals/backend/auto_start.py:254, report_generation/*.py, temporal/agentic/*.py) passing a real report id. The suggested fix ("verify report exists and belongs to team_id") is therefore already enforced at the only user write path.
votes.refutation: Refutation succeeded: the "any string" forgery route does not exist because the CharField at serializers.py:1746 never reaches `Task.signal_report`; it lands in `TaskRun.state`, which `find_signal_implementation_run` does not read. The only residual behaviour (a team member links a genuine same-team report to their own task through the validated FK) is not fixed by the finding's own suggestion (existence + team check already passes for such rows), and is further bounded by the stamphog carve-out gates the finding does not challenge: bot-authored PR (stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:169-172), repo-native head only (:176-178), enabled/synced repo config (:179-186), team recheck (:199-200), and the acting-reviewer resolver failing closed to `_InboxCarveOut(opted_out=True)` unless an opted-in reviewer exists for that report (:201-207). The outcome in that bounded case is a real review of the real diff, not an unearned approval. Claim rests on a premise the code contradicts, so it is not a real defect.

votes.evidence:
The finding's premise is that `TaskRunCreateRequestSerializer.signal_report_id` (a plain CharField, products/tasks/backend/presentation/serializers.py:1746-1751) feeds the `task.signal_report_id` that `find_signal_implementation_run` gates on (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:508). It does not. In both run-create facade paths the value goes only into the run's `extra_state` dict: facade/api.py:3030 reads it and 3047-3060 writes it into `extra_state["signal_report_id"]`; facade/api.py:4394 and 4476-4489 do the same via `runtime_state_fields`. Neither path assigns to `Task.signal_report`.

The Task FK is settable only through `TaskWriteSerializer.signal_report`, a `PrimaryKeyRelatedField` (serializers.py:435-441) whose queryset is bound in `__init__` to the real `SignalReport` manager (serializers.py:565-568, facade/api.py:3361-3367), so every accepted value is an existing report row, and `validate_signal_report` (serializers.py:611-614) rejects reports from another team. The update path pops `signal_report` entirely (facade/api.py:3828-3830), so it is set-once at creation. Server-side creators (`Task._build_task`, models.py:566; `signals/backend/auto_start.py:254`, `report_generation/*.py`) pass real report ids.

Existing tests already cover exactly what the suggestion asks for: `test_create_task_with_signal_report_different_team_rejected` (products/tasks/backend/tests/test_api.py:1388-1403) asserts a 400 for a cross-team report, and `test_non_qualifying_runs_return_none` (products/tasks/backend/tests/test_webhooks.py:1285-1320) parameterizes the internal-task, no-report, other-team and fork cases for `find_signal_implementation_run`. The stamphog carve-out additionally re-checks `run.team_id != repo_config.team_id` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:198-200) and fails closed when the acting-reviewer resolver returns None (tasks.py:201-207).
votes.refutation: Refutation succeeds. The "any string in signal_report_id" trigger does not exist: the unvalidated CharField the finding cites never reaches `Task.signal_report`; it only lands in `TaskRun.state`, which `find_signal_implementation_run` never reads. The FK that the function does read is already constrained to an existing, same-team `SignalReport` by `PrimaryKeyRelatedField` plus `validate_signal_report`, which is precisely the validation the suggestion proposes adding, and it is already tested. The residual "a team member can link their own task to some real report in their own team" is within-tenant, is not fixed by the suggested check (existence + team membership already passes for such rows), and still has to clear the bot-authored/repo-native/synced-config/opted-in-reviewer gates before it yields anything, and what it yields is a real review of the actual diff. No reachable defect remains.

votes.refutation: The trigger "any string in signal_report_id" is unreachable in production: the unvalidated CharField only populates run state, and the identification primitive reads the Task FK, which can only hold an existing, team-scoped SignalReport id (DB FK plus `validate_signal_report`). The finding's suggested fix (verify the report exists and belongs to team_id) is already what the write path enforces, so it would change nothing. The residual behavior, a team member linking a real report from their own team to their own task via the validated `TaskWriteSerializer.signal_report`, is intra-tenant, is still gated downstream (review_hog receivers.py:98-111 resolve an opted-in acting reviewer per report and fail closed), and is not what the finding describes. Premise contradicted by the code; not a real defect.
